title: Full pelvic (sacral) range of flexion at maximal forward flexion, by sex and age

quantity.name: pelvic (sacral) range of flexion
quantity.definition: angle at maximal flexion minus angle in relaxed standing. Lumbar angle = sum of Epionics segments lordotic in standing (lordosis negative, kyphosis positive); sacrum orientation = accelerometer angle vs gravity (pelvis surrogate). Full RoF = value at max (lumbar+sacrum) minus standing. Phase L/P = incremental lumbar change / incremental sacral change over 0-33% (early), 33-66% (middle), 66-100% (late) of total flexion (sum of both angles).

source.authors: Pries E, Dreischarf M, Bashkuev M, Putzier M, Schmidt H
source.sample: 309 subjects (134 M, 175 F); asymptomatic volunteers, BMI<26, age 20-75 (subset of the Consmuller 2012 cohort of 429); age groups 20-35 (n=155), 36-50 (n=100), >50 (n=54) (file K02_Pries2015.pdf)

protocol.summary: Full pelvic (sacral) RoF in 309 asymptomatic adults (Epionics), entire cohort (Table 1), by sex (Table 3) and sex x age (Table 2).
how_to_use: Use as the end-of-range pelvic (sacral) rotation for a subject of matching sex/age (mean, SD).

Aging: lumbar RoF falls (~-9 deg males, -6.5 deg females, 20-35 vs >50) while pelvic RoF rises (+12.8 deg males, +3.0 deg females); the change comes from the standing start posture, not the end posture.
Females use ~14 deg more pelvic rotation than males at equal lumbar RoF.

measurement.device: Epionics SPINE: 2 paravertebral strain-gauge strips (12 x 2.5 cm segments) 7.5 cm lateral of midline + tri-axial accelerometer at PSIS level (sacrum orientation)
measurement.task: 5 x maximal upper-body forward flexion from relaxed standing at preferred speed

protocol.notes: Age-group x sex n not reported (age groups total 155/100/54).

extraction.check_notes: All values re-read from rendered Table 2 and layout text of Table 3.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
